specification.problem: Reconstruct two Grover-algorithm questions: (1) a quantum model of an unordered phone book (quantum database) with programmable queries to search for a number or a name; (2) how successful Grover search is when the number of database elements is not precisely known, analyzed via distinguishability of states arising during Grover's algorithm using unambiguous discrimination.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small finite instance: standard Grover iteration on N items with one marked item, plus a mismatch analysis where the true database size differs from the guessed size. The detailed phone-book encoding and the discrimination success formula are not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Grover state after k iterations
equations.description: Standard single-marked-item Grover state in the marked/unmarked-superposition basis.
equations.justification: Textbook Grover analysis; the abstract does not give formulas.
assumptions: N known to define the oracle and diffusion

equations.label: Optimal iteration count
equations.description: Approximate iteration count maximizing success probability for known N.
equations.justification: Standard background for the optimal guess in the size-uncertainty question.

equations.label: Distinguishability of states
equations.description: Overlap of Grover states for true size N versus guessed size N', which governs unambiguous discrimination success.
equations.justification: The abstract says the question reduces to distinguishability of states; the overlap as the quantity is an assumed formalization.

registers.name: index
registers.role: database address register searched by Grover

registers.name: anc
registers.role: oracle phase-kickback ancilla; phone-book data/query registers not specified in abstract

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle^{\otimes n} on index, ancilla in |-\rangle; Hadamards on index give uniform superposition over N items (assuming N=2^n).

steps.description: Prepare uniform superposition over the index register with Hadamards.
Repeat k times: apply the programmable oracle marking the queried entry (by number or by name), then the diffusion operator about the uniform state.
For the size-uncertainty analysis, choose k from a guessed size N' and compare the resulting state with the true-N state via their overlap.

specification.measurement: Search: measure the index register in the computational basis after k iterations; the outcome is the address of the marked entry (then read out the name or number). Size-uncertainty: apply an unambiguous state discrimination POVM between the Grover states for candidate sizes, with outcomes 'state A', 'state B' or 'inconclusive'; for two equiprobable pure states the success probability is at most 1-|<psi|phi>| (assumed).
specification.classical_postprocessing: For search, verify the returned entry via a classical lookup and repeat on failure. For discrimination, tally conclusive vs inconclusive outcomes to estimate success rate and compare guessed N' against the true N using the overlap.
assumptions: N=2^n and one oracle ancilla in the circuit sketch.
Two-state equiprobable unambiguous discrimination (Ivanovic-Dieks-Peres bound) assumed for the measurement.
missing_information: Quantum phone book encoding and programmable query construction (number vs name oracle).
Exact unambiguous discrimination setup, states discriminated, POVM and success rates.
